title: Applying Insurance Actuarial Models to Price Correlated AI Failure Risk

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain from insurance pricing to regulatory pressure, but there is a gap in how beginner CS students would obtain reliable empirical inter-model correlation data to parameterize the actuarial models.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires actuarial mathematics (copula-based aggregate loss distributions) that is advanced and outside the typical CS curriculum. Beginners would struggle with the statistical finance framework even with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires both obtaining empirical correlation estimates from adversarial attack transferability and building actuarial models. Two substantial workstreams make this sustained effort rather than tightly scoped for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Copula-based actuarial models exist for cyber-insurance pricing, and AI is being used to improve insurance risk modeling. However, no existing work applies actuarial models specifically to price correlated AI model failure risk, using inter-model similarity/homogeneity data to parameterize copula-based aggregate loss distributions. The specific application to AI ecosystem correlated failures is novel, though the methodology is borrowed from established actuarial science.

evidence.source: Copula Based Actuarial Model for Pricing Cyber-Insurance Policies (SSRN)
evidence.finding: Uses copula-based actuarial models for cyber-insurance pricing, demonstrating the methodology applied to cyber risk—but for traditional cybersecurity, not AI-specific correlated failures.

evidence.source: Insurance Risk Modelling with Quantum-AI Copulas (2025)
evidence.finding: Advances copula modeling with quantum-AI for complex dependency structures in insurance, but applies AI to improve actuarial models rather than pricing AI failure risk.
